newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Accord in sight on television directive.
newsitem.headline: Accord in sight on television directive.

text.p: The Committee of Permanent Representatives meets on Wednesday to finalise its position ahead of next week's conciliation procedure on the television without frontiers directive.
On the table will be a new European Parliament proposal aimed at settling the last outstanding points to an accord.
The parliament proposal, an initiative of Culture Committee Chairman Peter Pex, aims to settle the last outstanding points separating the two institutions -- the parliament's amendments nine and 20.

Those amendments relate to the parliament's demand that people should have the right to see major events -- both sporting and cultural -- free when the exclusive rights to these are snapped up by pay television channels.

The Pex proposal was accepted by the parliamentary delegation to the conciliation committee on Tuesday and if accepted by COREPER on Wednesday will clear the pitch for a quick result at the start of the conciliation procedure on April 16.

"I think that as far as I am concerned the ball is in the Council's court," Pex told Reuters on Wednesday. "I really am very optimistic that next week we can come to an agreement and it will be easy."
